title: Power Rankings: Cavs finish on top
heading: 2009-10 Power Rankings: Week 24
author: Marc Stein

rankings.summaryHtml: Couldn't have been more wrong here. Thought the Cavs were destined for one of the longest regular seasons ever. Turns out life is always good with LeBron ... even when you're not sure how much longer he'll be around.

rankings.summaryHtml: You might be right if you say we've done the Magic wrong. Only once in 24 weeks have they ranked No. 1, but they're tops in the league since the All-Star break (21-5). The Cavs and Lakers aren't in the top five on that list.

rankings.summaryHtml: Just a shade behind Orlando for the league's best record since the All-Star break at 21-6, Phoenix keeps winning without Robin Lopez. The Suns, though, would be the first to say it'll be harder to do that in the playoffs.

rankings.summaryHtml: Never imagined a final batch of rankings that had the reigning champs so low. But I'd say we're still being plenty respectful when you add up L.A.'s 15-11 mark since the All-Star break to 5-9 against other division winners.

rankings.summaryHtml: Think the resurgent Jazz will be kicking themselves if they don't wind up finishing No. 2 in the West? No. 30 Minnesota has beaten only three teams more than once this season: New Jersey, Sacramento ... and Utah.

rankings.summaryHtml: How tough an out will the Spurs be without any further injuries? They're tied for second best in the West in average point margin and just set an NBA record by finishing with a winning road record for the 13th straight season.

rankings.summaryHtml: History says point differential is a big deal, so the Mavs can't ignore that theirs is by far the lowest of any West playoff team. Yet I'd also submit that no one is finishing second in this West without something clicking.

rankings.summaryHtml: Instead of reveling in a nationally televised W on the Lakers' floor -- with Kobe deciding to play and then misfiring in crunch time -- Portland is (what else?) sweating over another injury. It's all about B-Roy's knee from here.

rankings.summaryHtml: Last week's drop was just for effect to reflect how rough things have been lately. Denver should still be favored in any series it has home-court advantage as long as K-Mart is back for good. With or without their coach.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Hawks are 1-6 against the East's top two entering a season-ender against the LeBron-less Cavs. We'll soon see if those numbers are more pertinent than notching 50 wins for the first time since 1997-98.

rankings.summaryHtml: The good news: Durant needs 26 ppg in two games to win the scoring title if LeBron doesn't play again. The bad news: OKC's collapse at Golden State lines Durant up for a playoff baptism against Kobe's Lakers.

rankings.summaryHtml: It would appear that the performance last month in Dallas that wowed me so did not resurrect the 2008 Celtics. It would appear that the creaky Celts are still feeling the after-effects of that display ... three weeks later.

rankings.summaryHtml: You're going to hear folks say that the Heat -- on this 10-1 finishing kick and with D-Wade rollin' -- should have finished higher here and can spring a first-round upset. We, however, can't get past that easy closing schedule.

rankings.summaryHtml: Larry Brown is taking his record eighth NBA club to the playoffs, but we're not sure if this helps or hurts karma-wise: The only expansion team since '88 to win its first-ever playoff series was ... the Charlotte-based Hornets.

rankings.summaryHtml: You can't, on one hand, give your ROY vote to a kid (even a lefty) shooting 37 percent from the field. But Jennings still has me second-guessing my pick, because you can't deny the effect he's had on a playoff team.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Bulls play Boston and Charlotte away to finish the season. The Raps go to Detroit and host New York. Toronto holds the tiebreaker, so Chicago needs the better record. Yet we still like the Bulls' chances. Questions?
